It includes current and non-current assets such as derivative instruments, South Korean tax deposits, operating leases, and investments, totaling $2,140 million in 2020. On the liabilities side, it outlines current and non-current liabilities including wages, income taxes, litigation costs, and pension plan liabilities, amounting to $5,017 million in 2020. The section also discusses ongoing tax appeals in South Korea and the implications of certain liabilities related to litigation and customer deposits.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Debt and Financial Obligations
children.summary: This section details Corning's debt as of December 31, 2020, including current and long-term debt figures, with a total long-term debt of $7.897 billion. It provides a breakdown of various debentures and notes, including their interest rates and maturity dates. The section also discusses debt maturities by year, highlighting significant repayments and issuances in 2020, such as the redemption of $100 million in debentures and the establishment of new loan facilities in Chinese yuan. Additionally, it notes the fair value of long-term debt and the absence of outstanding commercial paper.

children.title: Corning Employee Retirement Plans Overview
children.summary: This section covers Corning's employee retirement plans, including defined benefit pension plans and postretirement benefits. It details the company's funding policies, contributions made in 2020, and obligations for healthcare and life insurance benefits. The funded status and changes in benefit obligations for defined benefit and postretirement plans are analyzed, with specific figures for service costs, interest costs, and actuarial gains or losses. Additionally, it discusses the impact of updated mortality assumptions and discount rates on financial health and benefit calculations.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Defined Benefit Plans
children.summary: This section details Corning's defined benefit pension plans for domestic and international employees, highlighting the company's funding policy to exceed minimum contribution requirements. In 2020, Corning made voluntary contributions of $180 million to domestic plans and $41 million to international plans, with plans for $31 million in 2021. It also discusses postretirement plans providing healthcare and life insurance benefits, including a cap on contributions for retiree medical coverage. Employees hired after January 1, 2007, will bear the full cost of their retiree medical benefits.

children.title: Pension Obligations and Funded Status Overview
children.summary: This section details the changes in benefit obligations and funded status of defined benefit pension plans for the years ending December 31, 2020, and 2019. It includes specific figures for service costs, interest costs, actuarial losses, and benefits paid, highlighting a total benefit obligation increase from $4,581 million in 2019 to $4,981 million in 2020. The fair value of plan assets also increased, resulting in a funded status of $(808) million at the end of 2020. Additionally, it provides insights into the projected and accumulated benefit obligations compared to the fair value of plan assets for various pension plans, indicating where obligations exceeded assets.

children.title: Overview of Postretirement Benefits and Financial Status
children.summary: This section details the changes in benefit obligations and funded status of postretirement plans, including specific figures for service costs, interest costs, and actuarial gains or losses for the years 2019 and 2020. It outlines the total net periodic benefit costs, including components such as service costs and interest costs, and highlights the impact of updated mortality assumptions on benefit obligations. Additionally, it discusses the discount rates used for calculating present values of projected benefit payments and the health care cost trend rates. Readers can learn about the financial health and assumptions underlying the company's postretirement benefits.

children.title: Overview of Plan Assets and Investment Strategy
children.summary: This section outlines the Company's strategy for managing plan assets to meet current and future obligations, emphasizing a target allocation of 40% in equity investments and 60% in bonds. It details the types of investments, including domestic and international stocks, corporate bonds, and fixed income assets, aimed at ensuring liquidity and mitigating interest rate sensitivity. The section also provides fair value measurement data for various asset categories, including Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 assets, and discusses risks associated with credit, currency, and liquidity. Additionally, it presents expected benefit payments for domestic and international pension plans and postretirement benefits for the upcoming years.

children.title: Asbestos and Environmental Liabilities Overview
children.summary: This section covers Corning's asbestos claims and liabilities, including those related to Pittsburgh Corning Corporation's Chapter 11 reorganization and Dow Corning's bankruptcy. It details financial reserves for non-PCC asbestos claims, breast implant litigation, and environmental liabilities under the Superfund Act. The section also discusses indemnity obligations and the financial implications of these claims, emphasizing the estimated reserves and the management's assessment of potential additional losses as remote.

children.title: Overview of Asbestos Claims and Liabilities
children.summary: This section details the asbestos claims involving Corning and PPG Industries, specifically related to Pittsburgh Corning Corporation (PCC) and its Chapter 11 reorganization plan effective April 2016, which included a $290 million liability. It also discusses non-PCC asbestos claims against Corning, with reserves estimated at $96 million as of December 31, 2020. Additionally, it covers Dow Corning's bankruptcy and related litigation, including breast implant claims and commercial creditor claims, with reserves and indemnity obligations outlined. The section provides insights into the financial implications and legal responsibilities of Corning regarding these claims.

children.title: Overview of Non-PCC Asbestos Claims Against Corning
children.summary: This section discusses non-PCC asbestos claims against Corning, which were stayed until the confirmation of the PCC reorganization plan in 2016. As of December 31, 2020, the reserve for these claims was estimated at $96 million, reflecting projected claims and legal fees. The section provides insights into the financial implications of these claims and their status following the lifting of the stay.

children.title: Dow Corning Bankruptcy and Indemnity Matters
children.summary: This section discusses the Chapter 11 bankruptcy matters related to Dow Corning Corporation, including the realignment of ownership between Corning and Dow, which occurred on May 31, 2016. It details Corning's indemnification agreement for Dow Corning's pre-closing liabilities and outlines the breast implant litigation that led to Dow Corning's bankruptcy filing in 1995. The section also mentions the establishment of a Settlement Trust and the financial reserves set aside for breast implant claims and other creditor claims, including a $107 million reserve for interest claims that were settled in 2019. Corning assesses that its indemnity obligations related to these matters are not expected to be material.

children.title: Overview of Dow Corning Breast Implant Litigation
children.summary: This section details the Dow Corning Breast Implant Litigation, highlighting the company's bankruptcy filing in May 1995 due to numerous lawsuits related to breast implants. It outlines the emergence from Chapter 11 in June 2004 with a Plan of Reorganization that included a Settlement Trust and Litigation Facility for claim resolution. Dow Corning has paid approximately $1.8 billion to the Settlement Trust and recorded a reserve of $290 million for litigation as of May 31, 2016, which was later adjusted to $160 million by December 31, 2020. The section also mentions potential indemnity obligations for Corning related to excess liabilities.

children.title: Dow Corning Bankruptcy Interest Claims Overview
children.summary: This section discusses the bankruptcy-related interest claims against Dow Corning, specifically from commercial creditors seeking additional compounded interest and legal fees from May 1995 to June 2004. As of May 31, 2016, Dow Corning had a recorded reserve of $107 million for these claims. The claims were settled by September 30, 2019, with bankruptcy court approval. Corning does not anticipate any material indemnity obligation related to these claims.

children.title: Dow Corning's Environmental Liabilities and Claims Overview
children.summary: This section details Dow Corning's environmental claims and liabilities, including a notification from Dow to Corning regarding potential losses from environmental remediation at various sites. It outlines Corning's responsibility under the Superfund Act for 15 hazardous waste sites and the accrued liabilities for environmental cleanup, which were approximately $68 million as of December 31, 2020. The section also discusses the company's policy for estimating these liabilities based on expert analysis and monitoring, indicating that the risk of additional losses is considered remote.

children.title: Corning's Environmental Litigation and Liability Overview
children.summary: This section discusses Corning's involvement in environmental litigation, specifically its designation as a potentially responsible party for 15 hazardous waste sites under the Superfund Act. It outlines Corning's policy to accrue estimated liabilities for environmental cleanup, with recorded amounts of approximately $68 million and $41 million for 2020 and 2019, respectively. The section emphasizes that management believes the accrued reserve is a reasonable estimate of liability and that the risk of additional losses is considered remote. Additionally, it mentions the indemnification agreement with Dow regarding environmental claims.

children.title: Impact of Hedging Activities on Financial Statements
children.summary: This section examines the effects of cash flow and undesignated hedges on Corning's consolidated financial statements from 2018 to 2020. It details the gains and losses recognized in other comprehensive income (OCI) and their subsequent reclassification into income, focusing on interest rate and foreign exchange contracts. The section highlights specific financial impacts, including a $14 million loss from the de-designation of certain cash flow hedges, and provides figures related to net sales, cost of sales, and other expenses. Overall, it illustrates the financial implications of these derivative instruments on the company's performance.

children.title: Impact of Cash Flow Hedges on Financial Statements
children.summary: This section details the impact of derivative financial instruments on Corning's consolidated financial statements for the years 2018-2020, specifically focusing on cash flow hedges. It includes tables summarizing gains and losses recognized in other comprehensive income (OCI) and their reclassification into income. The section highlights the financial effects of designated hedges, such as interest rate and foreign exchange contracts, and notes a specific loss from the de-designation of certain cash flow hedges. Readers can learn about the financial implications of these hedges on net sales and expenses over the specified years.

children.title: Impact of Undesignated Hedges on Financial Statements
children.summary: This section provides a summary of the effects of Corning's derivative financial instruments on its consolidated financial statements for the years ended December 31, 2018-2020. It details the gains and losses recognized in other comprehensive income (OCI) and the reclassification of these amounts into income for both designated and undesignated hedges. The section highlights specific figures for net sales, cost of sales, and other expenses related to foreign exchange and interest rate hedges. Additionally, it notes a loss of $14 million from the de-designation of certain cash flow hedges, emphasizing the impact of these financial instruments on the company's financial performance.

children.title: Fair Value Measurements and Financial Performance Overview
children.summary: This section details Corning Incorporated's fair value measurements, including the calculation of basic and diluted earnings per common share, share-based compensation plans, and stock options valuation. It provides a reconciliation of earnings per share from 2018 to 2020, outlines the company's long-term incentive plans, and discusses the financial implications of stock options using the Black-Scholes model. Additionally, it covers incentive stock plans with a focus on restricted stock units and their associated costs, as well as an overview of reportable segments and their financial performance from 2018 to 2020.

children.title: Calculation of Earnings Per Common Share
children.summary: This section explains the calculation of basic and diluted earnings per common share for Corning Incorporated. Basic earnings are derived from net income attributable to common shareholders divided by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding. Diluted earnings consider the potential issuance of additional shares from dilutive securities. The section provides a reconciliation of net income and shares outstanding for the years 2018 to 2020, detailing figures for basic and diluted earnings per share, as well as the impact of convertible preferred stock and stock options on these calculations.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Share-Based Compensation Plans
children.summary: Corning has established long-term incentive plans for key employees and board members, allowing for various equity-based compensation awards such as stock options and performance share units. As of December 31, 2020, approximately 36 million common shares were available for future grants under these plans. In 2020, Corning increased the equity component of its Long-Term Incentive Plan from 40% to 75% of an executive's annual compensation. The costs associated with share-based compensation are allocated across multiple expense lines in the consolidated statements of income.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Stock Options and Valuation
children.summary: This section covers the financial aspects of stock options granted by Corning, detailing the weighted-average grant-date fair value, total fair value of vested options, and associated compensation costs for the years 2018 to 2020. It also discusses unrecognized compensation costs as of December 31, 2020, and proceeds from option exercises. The Black-Scholes valuation model is explained, including its inputs such as expected volatility, dividends, and risk-free rates.

children.title: Stock Options Financial Overview and Valuation
children.summary: This section provides detailed financial data regarding stock options granted by Corning for the years ending December 31, 2020, 2019, and 2018. It includes the weighted-average grant-date fair value of options, total fair value of vested options, and compensation costs associated with stock options. Additionally, it outlines the unrecognized compensation costs as of December 31, 2020, and the proceeds from option exercises. The section also describes the Black-Scholes valuation model used for estimating fair value, including inputs such as expected volatility, dividends, and risk-free rates.

children.title: Incentive Stock Plans Overview
children.summary: This section covers the Company's incentive stock plans, focusing on time-based and performance-based restricted stock units (RSUs) as of December 31, 2020. It details the number of non-vested shares, grant-date fair values, and unrecognized compensation costs, totaling approximately $149 million for time-based units and $32 million for performance-based units. The expected recognition period for time-based units is 2.4 years, while performance-based RSUs are earned based on specific targets and typically vest over three years. The total compensation cost for performance-based RSUs for the year was approximately $81 million, influenced by retirement-eligible employees.

children.title: Overview of Time-Based and Performance-Based Stock Units
children.summary: This section provides a detailed overview of the Company's non-vested time-based restricted stock and restricted stock units as of December 31, 2020, including the number of shares, grant-date fair values, and changes from the previous year. It highlights the unrecognized compensation costs associated with these arrangements, totaling approximately $149 million, and outlines the expected recognition period of 2.4 years. Additionally, it discusses performance-based restricted stock units, including their grant details, vesting conditions, and associated compensation costs, which amounted to approximately $81 million for the year ended December 31, 2020.

children.title: Overview of Performance-Based Restricted Stock Units
children.summary: This section details the status and financial implications of performance-based restricted stock units (RSUs) as of December 31, 2020. It outlines the number of non-vested shares, their grant-date fair value, and changes during the year, including grants, forfeitures, and the total unrecognized compensation cost of approximately $32 million. The section explains that these RSUs are earned based on achieving specific performance targets and are typically vested over three years, with compensation costs recognized over the vesting period. Additionally, it notes that the compensation cost for the year was approximately $81 million, influenced by retirement-eligible employees.

children.title: Overview of Reportable Segments and Financial Performance
children.summary: This section outlines the reportable segments of the company, including Display Technologies, Optical Communications, Specialty Materials, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences, detailing their specific manufacturing focuses. It also describes the 'All Other' category, which includes segments not meeting reporting thresholds and the impact of the acquisition of HSG. Financial results for each segment are presented, including net sales, depreciation, research and development expenses, and net income for the years 2018-2020. Additionally, it discusses the exclusion of certain foreign currency impacts from segment results and provides reconciliations of segment net income to consolidated net income.

children.title: CEO Certification Under Sarbanes-Oxley Act
children.summary: This section contains the certification by Wendell P. Weeks, the Chief Executive Officer of Corning Incorporated, as required by Section 302(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. It confirms that he has reviewed the Annual Report on Form 10-K and asserts that the report is free of material misstatements. The certification also details the responsibilities for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting, including evaluations of their effectiveness and disclosures of any significant deficiencies or fraud. This certification is a key component of corporate governance and financial accountability.

children.title: CFO Certification Under Sarbanes-Oxley Act
children.summary: This section contains the certification by R. Tony Tripeny, Chief Financial Officer of Corning Incorporated, in compliance with Section 302(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. It confirms the review of the annual report on Form 10-K, asserts the accuracy of the financial statements, and outlines responsibilities regarding disclosure controls and internal financial reporting. The certification includes an evaluation of the effectiveness of these controls and discloses any significant deficiencies or fraud related to financial reporting. The date of certification is February 12, 2021.

children.title: CEO Certification Under Sarbanes-Oxley Act
children.summary: This section contains the certification by Wendell P. Weeks, CEO, and R. Tony Tripeny, CFO, of Corning Incorporated, affirming compliance with 18 U.S.C. Section 1350 and the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. They certify that the company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2020, meets the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Additionally, they assert that the information in the report accurately reflects the company's financial condition and operational results.
